title: Optimistic vs Pessimistic Locking
subtitle: Preventing lost updates and double-booking in high-concurrency reservation and inventory systems.
keyTakeaways: Pessimistic locking acquires exclusive database locks (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`), preventing concurrent transactions from touching the row until the transaction commits.
Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) uses a version column to detect conflicting updates at commit time, holding zero database locks during processing.
Use pessimistic locking when write contention is high (concert ticket drops); use optimistic locking when contention is low (editing user profiles).
architectureDiagram:
OPTIMISTIC VS PESSIMISTIC LOCKING MECHANICS
PESSIMISTIC LOCKING (High Contention / Lock Row Immediately):
Client A: BEGIN -> SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (Lock Acquired) -------------> UPDATE -> COMMIT (Lock Released)
Client B: BEGIN -> SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (BLOCKED! Waits on lock) ---> UPDATE -> COMMIT

OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY CONTROL (Low Contention / Version Check):
Client A: Read row (v=1) -> Computes -> UPDATE ... WHERE id=1 AND v=1 (Succeeds! v becomes 2)
Client B: Read row (v=1) -> Computes -> UPDATE ... WHERE id=1 AND v=1 (0 rows updated! Conflict -> Retries)

sections.heading: Pessimistic Locking and Deadlock Prevention
sections.body: Pessimistic locking assumes conflicts are likely. The moment a transaction reads a row it intends to modify, it acquires an exclusive lock via `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`. Any concurrent transaction attempting to read or modify that row is blocked by the database engine until the holding transaction commits or rolls back.
bullets: Eliminates Lost Updates: Guarantees that only one thread can inspect and mutate state at any given moment.

The Risk of Deadlocks: If Transaction 1 locks Account A then attempts to lock Account B, while Transaction 2 locks Account B and attempts to lock Account A, both block indefinitely. The database detects the deadlock and aborts one transaction.
Deadlock Prevention Rule: Always lock resources in a globally consistent order (e.g., sorting account IDs in ascending alphanumeric order before issuing locks).
Lock Contention Bottleneck: Hot rows (like a single inventory counter for a Taylor Swift concert) will queue thousands of transactions, exhausting connection pools.

sections.heading: Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) and Retry Loops
sections.body: Optimistic locking assumes conflicts are rare. Transactions hold zero database locks during processing. Instead, each row includes a `version` integer or timestamp. When updating, the transaction verifies that the version in the database matches the version read initially. If another transaction updated the row in the interim, the version check fails, returning zero updated rows.
bullets: Zero Lock Contention: Read operations execute without holding locks, preserving maximum read and write concurrency.
Application Retry Loops: When an update returns 0 affected rows, the application catches the conflict, re-reads the fresh row version, and retries the business operation.
Thundering Herd Vulnerability: If 1,000 requests attempt to update the same row under OCC, 1 will succeed and 999 will fail and retry, flooding the database with wasted CPU work.

tradeOffs.pros: Guaranteed success for the lock holder; ideal when rollback cost is high or contention is severe; prevents wasted compute.
tradeOffs.cons: Risk of deadlocks; holds database locks across network round trips; exhausts connection pools under heavy load.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Flash sale inventory reservation, seat booking, banking transfers, and warehouse fulfillment.

tradeOffs.pros: Zero blocking locks; highest throughput when conflicts are rare; works seamlessly across disconnected user sessions.
tradeOffs.cons: Massive write contention causes high retry churn and wasted database CPU cycles.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Content management systems, user profile edits, document collaboration, and low-contention CRUD APIs.

interviewTip: In high-concurrency ticket or inventory problems, state your locking strategy explicitly: 'Because write contention on seats is intense, optimistic locking would cause 99% of requests to fail and retry, overwhelming the database. We will use pessimistic locking with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` and enforce strict alphabetical lock ordering across row IDs to eliminate deadlocks.'
